title: Predictive prefetch and sticky session allocator — design
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose
This design specifies an allocator and prefetch coordinator for ephemeral conversational sessions that: 1) reduces cold-start latency for in-flight sessions, 2) improves KV-prefix hit rate through predictive prefetching, and 3) provides tenant-aware stickiness to preserve low-latency affinity without compromising multi-tenant fairness.

Scope
- Applies to hosted and dedicated runtime paths for conversational and interactive workloads.
- Affects runtime request router, session store, KV-prefetch cache, and the autoscaler / placement decision logic.
- Does NOT change model execution kernels or lower-level GPU scheduling primitives.

Goals
- Reduce median first-token latency for resumed conversational sessions by 20–40% for workloads with >10% session reactivation.
- Increase KV cache rehydration hit rate by 30% for typical conversation patterns (short bursts + user pauses).
- Maintain tenant isolation and SLO fairness: no tenant should see >5% regression in p50 latency due to prefetching activity from another tenant.

Non-goals
- This design is not a full replacement for long-term embedding caching or vector-store strategies.
- We will not attempt cross-tenant prompt content pre-warming for private deployments.

Design summary (short)
We introduce two cooperating components: the Sticky Session Allocator (SSA) and the Predictive Prefetch Coordinator (PPC). SSA assigns a soft affinity between session IDs and serving shards (or lanes) based on historical run-length, tenant policy, and locality. PPC monitors session lifecycle signals and model KV-access patterns to schedule prefetch jobs that warm the runtime KV cache before a scheduled request reaches the serving lane. Both components respect a tenant-level budget and global admission-control penalties to avoid destabilizing capacity.

Architecture and components
1) Sticky Session Allocator (SSA)\- Responsibility: maintain soft mappings session_id -> serving lane with TTL and decay.\- Inputs: session activity history, tenant policy (stickiness allowed/disabled), lane load metrics, placement scores.\- Outputs: affinity token assigned to requests, fallback policy for when the lane is unavailable.\- Behaviour: affinity tokens have weight (0..1) and expire after idle_period or max_ttl. We bias new requests with the token when route selection occurs.

2) Predictive Prefetch Coordinator (PPC)\- Responsibility: create prefetch tasks to hydrate KV cache / prefix buffers for a session before expected resume.\- Inputs: session idle interval, prior sequence length distribution, model variant, per-tenant prefetch budget, time-series of request inter-arrival times.\- Outputs: prefetch jobs (small n-context forward passes or KV fetches), estimated cost, and result status (hydrated/failed).

3) Admission & Budgeting Layer
- Global governor that enforces: max_prefetch_concurrency, per-tenant_budget_tokens, and pref_overcommit_threshold.
- Prefetch tasks consume budget tokens proportional to estimated token rehydration cost.

Data flows
1. On request end, SSA updates session metadata: last_active_ts, average_turn_length, preferred_lane.
2. When a session exceeds idle_min_threshold, PPC evaluates reactivation probability using an exponential-decay predictor (see Predictor section).
3. If probability > prefetch_threshold and tenant budget allows, PPC schedules a prefetch to run into the targeted lane.
4. Prefetch results (success/failure, bytes warmed, KV hit probability) are written to session metadata for routing heuristics.

Predictor model (heuristic + ML hybrid)
- Baseline: Exponential decay + time-of-day buckets + last-turn-length feature. This is fast and transparent.
- Optional: Lightweight logistic regression (server-side) trained on historical session traces to improve probability estimates for enterprise tenants who opt in.
- Features used: idle_seconds, avg_turn_tokens, tenant_id, app_route, last_5_intervals_mean, day_of_week, hour_of_day.

API contracts and route changes
- New request header: X-Session-Affinity-Token: <token> (opaque string). Provided by SSA for clients that manage sessions.
- New admin API: POST /admin/prefetch/{session_id} to trigger an ad-hoc prefetch (used by customer connectors).
- Runtime routing changes: routing path will prefer lanes with matching affinity tokens unless lane load exceeds overload_threshold.

Configuration and constraints (table)
| Setting | Default | Purpose | Range / Notes |
| max_prefetch_concurrency | "2000" | Global concurrency limit for prefetch tasks | integer >= 100 |
| tenant_prefetch_budget_per_min | "10" | Tokens per tenant per minute | integer, adjustable per contract |
| prefetch_probability_threshold | "0.65" | Min predicted resume probability to trigger prefetch | 0.5–0.95 |
| ttl_affinity_seconds | "3600" | Default sticky TTL for SSA token | 60–86400 |
| pref_overcommit_threshold | "1.2" | Allowed overcommit factor when capacity is idle | 1.0–2.0 |

Example YAML config snippet
server:
  allocator:
    ttl_affinity_seconds: 3600
    max_affinities_per_lane: 5000
  prefetch:
    max_prefetch_concurrency: 2000
    tenant_prefetch_budget_per_min: 10
    prefetch_probability_threshold: 0.65

Prefetch task sketch (pseudo)
1. Reserve budget token.
2. Select target lane = SSA.preferred_lane(session_id) or best_lane_by_cost().
3. Execute warm-forward with small window of tokens or explicit KV fetch (implementation varies by model).
4. Validate resulting KV size and write metadata: hydrated=true, hydrated_at=ts.
5. Release budget token.

Rollout plan and safety knobs
Phase 0 (Canary):
- Enable SSA affinity header passthrough only for internal dev tenants. No prefetching. Monitor routing churn and lane imbalance metrics for 2 weeks.
Phase 1 (Prefetch pilot):
- Enable PPC in simulated mode (decisions logged but not executed) for a subset of traffic to calibrate predictors.
Phase 2 (Soft launch):
- Enable real prefetch for 5% of production sessions. Enforce strict tenant budgets and global max_prefetch_concurrency=200. Observe p50/p95 latency, KV hit rate, and tail CPU/GPU utilization.
Phase 3 (Scale):
- Gradually scale to 25%, then 100% for tenants flagged as safe. Ramp budgets per-tenant after manual review.

Safety knobs (run-time):
- global_prefetch_pause (boolean): immediately pause new prefetch tasks.
- tenant_quarantine (list): temporary block list for tenants causing overload.
- emergency_eviction: if lane overload > 85% for 5m, evict prefetched context to free resources.

Metrics and SLOs (recommended)
- KPI: session_resume_first_token_latency_p50/p95 (goal: -20% p50 for resumed sessions).
- KPI: kv_prefetch_hit_rate_by_session (goal: +30% from baseline).
- Safety: prefetch_cpu_fraction, prefetch_gpu_fraction (should be < 5% under normal ops).
- Alert: tenant_prefetch_budget_burn_rate > 2x baseline for 10m.

Operational runbook (high level)
1. Detect: pager alert fires for prefetch-related overload (CPU/GPU > threshold).
2. Triage: identify lanes and tenant ids from prefetch metrics dashboard.
3. Mitigate: toggle global_prefetch_pause=true and set tenant_quarantine for offending tenants.
4. Recover: let system stabilize, analyze traces, then re-enable with reduced budgets.
5. Postmortem: if outage, follow standard incident process and record regression metrics.

Testing and validation plan
- Unit tests for SSA weight decay and token issuance.
- Integration test: simulated traffic with varied idle intervals to measure prefetch effectiveness.
- Load test: measure global_prefetch_concurrency behaviour under synthetic spikes.
- A/B experiment: route 50/50 sessions to prefetch-enabled vs baseline runtime and compare latency, cost, and cache hit metrics.

Security and privacy considerations
- Prefetching only uses session metadata and KV-index pointers; we do not include customer prompt content in cross-tenant prefetch tasks.
- For private deployments, PPC is disabled unless explicitly allowed by customer config.
- All prefetch audit logs are written to tenant-scoped retention buckets and accessible only to authorized roles.

Cost and pricing implications
- Prefetching will increase short-term token-equivalent compute. We propose adding a tiered "prefetch credit" SKU for Dedicated tenants that opt for aggressive prefetch budgets. Pricing guidance: base included budget (10 tokens/min), additional credits billed at measured token-equivalent cost.

Open questions and trade-offs
- Do we allow cross-tenant opportunistic prefetching when lane utilization is low? Tradeoff: better aggregate hit rate vs. tenant isolation concerns.
- How to model complex multi-turn dialogue where prefetching a wrong prefix can increase cost without improving latency? Conservative thresholds and quick failure detection recommended.

Ownership and next steps
- Feature owner: Aisha Patel (serving runtime).
- Implementation sprint plan: 3 sprints for SSA, 4 sprints for PPC, 2 sprints for dashboarding and safety knobs.
- Next steps: prototype predictor in the lab, create simulated-trace runner, and submit an API contract PR for X-Session-Affinity-Token.

Appendix: sample CLI and traces
# Trigger an admin prefetch (dev-only)
curl -X POST "https://api.internal.redwood.io/admin/prefetch/SESSION_1234" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"target_lane": "lane-east-1-a", "mode":"kv"}'

Sample trace record (logged)
- session_id: SESSION_1234
- event: prefetch_scheduled
- predictor_score: 0.72
- target_lane: lane-east-1-a
- budget_token_id: TB_9876
- result: hydrated
